prompt: A page-layout proof: a single upright A4 page (210 mm wide, 297 mm tall) shown on a plain grey backdrop, with a millimetre RULER along the top edge and down the left edge of the page (numbered every 50 mm). On the page is one rectangular block of body text (grey lines of placeholder text). The four page margins — the white space between the edge of the sheet and the text block — must be set to these EXACT, deliberately UNEQUAL values: TOP margin 19 mm, BOTTOM margin 31 mm, LEFT margin 34 mm, RIGHT margin 16 mm. So the text block is pushed to the right (the left binding margin 34 mm is much wider than the right margin 16 mm) and sits higher than centre (top 19 mm is smaller than bottom 31 mm). Print a small key in the top-left of the page reading 'Page margins (mm): TOP = 19  BOTTOM = 31  LEFT = 34  RIGHT = 16'. The ACTUAL white space on each side of the text block must match its printed label exactly when measured against the ruler. Do NOT centre the text block; the margins are unequal. Clean print, black text on white page, thin ruler ticks.
